name: Akira Arcade
subtitle: Delta for iPad, with phones as game controllers.
description: Akira Arcade is a community fork of Delta by Riley Testut, made for Akira, a retro-computer dock for the iPad. Phones on the same Wi-Fi scan a QR code and their browser becomes a gamepad.

apps.name: Akira Arcade
apps.developerName: Akira · fork of Delta by Riley Testut
apps.subtitle: Your phone is the controller.
apps.localizedDescription:
Play classic games on your iPad with up to 4 phones as controllers. Open Phone Controller from the pause menu, scan the QR code with a phone on the same Wi-Fi, and the phone's browser becomes a gamepad styled after the console being played: NES, SNES, Game Boy / Color / Advance, DS, Mega Drive and N64 (with a thumb stick).

Built on Delta 2.0 by Riley Testut (AGPLv3). Source: https://github.com/yamustofa/akira-arcade

Akira Arcade ships no games or BIOS files.

versions.localizedDescription: Akira Arcade 0.1.0: phones as game controllers, console-styled pads, N64 thumb stick, up to 4 phones, Join Wi-Fi QR. Notes: https://github.com/yamustofa/akira-arcade/blob/main/docs/akira/releases/v0.1.0.md

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: Delta uses the local network to communicate with AltServer, enable JIT, connect to Epilogue Operator devices, and let phones on the same Wi-Fi act as game controllers.
privacy.NSMicrophoneUsageDescription: Delta uses your microphone to emulate the Nintendo DS microphone.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription: Please allow Delta to save screenshots to your Photo Library.
privacy.NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription: Press “OK” to allow Delta to use images from your Photo Library as game artwork.
